thread:
aj: Heads up — seeing duplicate billing events when clients reconnect after idle. Not consistent, but spikes correlate with our streaming resume window.

maria: ugh. can you paste an example log? timestamp + request id helps.

aj: here's a trimmed trace: 
```
2026-11-12T10:12:33Z stream.start req=rp_42 user=u-77 model=redwood-large
2026-11-12T10:12:47Z stream.resume req=rp_42 resume_id=ev_998
2026-11-12T10:12:47Z stream.start req=rp_43 user=u-77 model=redwood-large
2026-11-12T10:12:47Z billing.message token_count=120 req=rp_43
2026-11-12T10:12:48Z billing.message token_count=120 req=rp_42
```
Two start/resume pairs for same user within ms. One shows up in console as a separate route-hit which then increments quota twice.

rachel: we already emit stream.resume and stream.start events separately — current dashboard treats them as independent billable starts. We should add a de-dup signal for resume diagnostics. Filed quick issue: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/streams/issue/423

kevin: question — is this a client-side double-reconnect (resume + open new) or server accepting both? If server accepts both then routing could send resume to canary and new connect to stable -> double-charge + mismatched variant.

aj: saw both cases. In some traces the client does send two attempts (old SDK w/o jitter). In others, a single resume gets accepted but our internal router also spawns a fresh session on mismatch fallback.

maria: two potential fixes: 1) server-side dedupe: mark resume_id as consumed once a session is resumed, return 409 on duplicate resume; 2) conservative routing: hold new session until resume window expires/confirmed. 3) enforce client jitter/backoff in SDKs.

kevin: server-side dedupe sounds safest for billing correctness but risky for backwards compat: some clients expect resume to be idempotent for failover. 409 will break legitimate retry flows.

rachel: telemetry note — we need a composite metric: stream.resume_successful_dedupe=false/true paired with billing.event_source=(resume|new). That will let us see how many billable duplicates are resume-originated. Also add tag: routing_variant (stable/canary).

ux-sara: UX: console should show a single session timeline when resume_id matches recent start. Right now timeline splits into two rows and it's confusing for customers. If we introduce resume_jitter knob, add a short tooltip: "Controls client reconnect jitter to reduce duplicate sessions during transient disconnects". Default on.

aj: example of client header when resuming: 
```
GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Accept: text/event-stream
Last-Event-ID: ev_998
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
```
If Last-Event-ID is present server should strongly prefer resume path and avoid creating a new session for same user/model until resume timed out.

maria: operationally, can we add short-term fix: server accepts resume but emits an audit tag and does not bill the resumed session until final ack from router? i.e., provisional session that becomes billable only after first token emitted. That avoids double billing if dedupe occurs quickly.

kevin: that feels like a good incremental path. We'll still need long-term: either make resume_id single-use (atomic consume) or change routing to stick by resume affinity.

rachel: I'll add the telemetry changes and dashboard rows. Quick query: 
```
count_by(metric="billing.message", group_by=["resume_used","routing_variant"]) | sort desc
```
should show duplicates.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: streaming/jitter-provisional-billing @staging — started 2026-11-12T11:00:00Z :rocket:

aj: note for rollout — canary must be pinned to same resume semantics. If canary has dedupe enabled and stable doesn't, users routed between the two will see odd behavior. Plan canary -> stable in lockstep.

ux-sara: I'll add a console warning in the rollout UX: "Changing resume behavior may impact clients on mixed runtimes; recommended: gradual rollout with telemetry on resume_dup_rate" and a preflight check that warns if any active dedicated customers have older SDK versions.

maria: action items: 
- rachel: add telemetry metrics + dashboard (ETA today)
- kevin: prototype provisional billing gating (ETA 2 days)
- aj: collect sample traces + SDK versions where double-reconnect observed (ETA today)
- ux-sara: update console rollout copy and add resume_jitter knob (ETA 3 days)

kevin: also adding a quick test harness for resume race: script will open many idle connections and force TCP resets to measure duplicate start rate.

aj: thanks. ping me if you want sample traces or to repro locally. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all — this one explains a few support tickets. adding to priority queue. :spiral_calendar:

deploy-bot: rollout status: streaming/jitter-provisional-billing @staging succeeded in 2/3 canary nodes — continuing to stable.
